incident.title: Transient S3 (ordinary) store restart during the first faithful postgres/S3 rerun
incident.detail: First attempt at the faithful full-file real-Postgres/S3 rerun (postgres-faithful.log) got 10 pass / 2 fail, both failures a raw AWS SDK InternalError (HTTP 500, $fault:'server', already retried 3x by the SDK) surfacing mid-request during the maximum-row-count case and one immediately after. docker inspect on ezcorp-factory-storage-1001-factory-storage-ordinary-1 showed StartedAt only ~17s before it was checked, fresh SeaweedFS startup log lines, ExitCode=0, OOMKilled=false, memory limit still correctly 2 GiB (not a regression of the earlier-documented OOM incident). This validator did not run compose, did not restart or reconfigure anything. Reported to the team lead immediately per instruction, then reran the identical command once bun scripts/verify-factory-storage.ts confirmed the store healthy again: the retry passed clean, 11 pass / 0 fail, matching the normal test count (the failed run showed 'Ran 12 tests' -- one extra anonymous failed entry attributable to a cascading cleanup/close() hitting the same outage). Conclusion: infrastructure blip, not a W12 code regression.

verificationChecklist.item: ReferenceDataGuestDirectory.create sets no mode/owner and runs no podman unshare
verificationChecklist.evidence: grep -rniE 'chmod|chown|unshare|0o7' across src/factory/reference-data/*.ts (excl. tests) and the two build scripts finds only one chmod(path, 0o644) on a per-file STAGED INPUT (materials.ts:147) and one comment describing what the RUNNER does; no chown, no unshare, no directory-mode chmod anywhere in production code. Direct diff read of materials.ts confirms the entire handOver-style block (mkdir of in/out, chmod(root), chmod(input dir), chmod(output,0o770), Bun.spawnSync podman unshare chown) was deleted; ReferenceDataGuestDirectory.create is now a two-line mkdtemp-and-return.

verificationChecklist.item: Tests asserting the pack's own chown are gone, replaced by cases proving a guest write succeeds against the runner's handover
verificationChecklist.evidence: materials.test.ts diff: the old 'per-attempt directory is laid out so a guest running as another user can read and write it' test (which asserted output.mode===0o770, output.uid!==process uid, output.gid===process gid) is replaced by 'the per-attempt directory is one flat directory the runner hands over, and this host sets no mode on it' (asserts only the staged input's mode, and that the ROOT directory's uid is still this host's, i.e. untouched pre-handover) plus a new 'only what the guest left is reported' test. pack.test.ts adds a guestWrote() helper that writes straight into the flat directory the way a real guest would (not through directory.stage(), which is host-only), and every existing pack-level test (report reading, digest mismatch, deadline, crash-mid-invocation, runner-refuses-to-start) now exercises that path. The 'host with no container runtime fails closed' test (which tested the OLD podman-unshare fallback) is removed, matching the removed code path. Genuine proof that a real uid-remapped guest can physically write is necessarily an integration-level fact, not a unit-test one; that is covered by the independently-rerun journey.integration.test.ts and the real postgres/S3 leg (both 11/0), plus the shared runner's own materials.test.ts/podman.integration.test.ts (Terra-owned, part of the 45/0 shared-runner-regression rerun) which directly test the new PodmanRunner.handOverMaterials().

verificationChecklist.item: collect()/produced() still go through shared listRunnerMaterials/openRunnerMaterial, boundary row intact
verificationChecklist.evidence: materials.ts diff shows the import line `import { GUEST_MATERIALS_PATH, listRunnerMaterials, openRunnerMaterial } from '@ezcorp/extension-runner'` is untouched; collect() still calls openProduced() -> openRunnerMaterial(), produced() still calls listRunnerMaterials(). scripts/check-factory-boundaries.ts:121-122 still carries both REQUIRED_SHARED_IMPORTS rows for src/factory/reference-data/materials.ts (packages/@ezcorp/extension-runner/src/index.ts and src/extensions/v4/blobs.ts), and the boundaries gate passes.

verdictRationale: Every item the round-3 instruction asked me to verify is independently confirmed against the actual diff and a clean rerun, not taken on the gate file's word. The one failure I hit (a real-services test failure) was root-caused to a transient S3 store restart coincident with, not caused by, this round's code changes -- confirmed by container inspection (graceful restart, not OOM, memory limit unchanged) and by a clean retry once the store was confirmed healthy again, with no store management performed by this validator at any point. All static gates, the full focused suite, the Python lane, both integration journeys (embedded and real), the expanded shared-runner regression (now including the runner's own new handover tests), and the coverage gates pass cleanly on a clean tree at head 23a7a6da3. No new findings. ACCEPT.
